To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

supramolecular bilayer membranes, each composed of peptide lipids having an (S )-alanine residue, a hydrophobically pyridoxal-derived compound, and copper( II ) ions, mediate the enantioselective aldolation of glycinate and benzaldehyde to give (S )-phenylserinate.
supramolecular bilayer membranes consisting of peptide lipids and pyridoxal derivatives catalyze aldol reactions with enantioselectivities that are comparable with those of natural enzymes.

the supramolecular assemblies of functionalized peptide lipids and a vitamin B6-derived cofactor, in combination with copper(II) ion, act as an artificial enzyme that catalyzes the aldolation reaction with high enantioselectivities.

the design, synthesis and evaluation of new, highly active, and selective organocatalysts based on chiral pyridoxal derivatives, which are able to catalyze the enantioselective aldol addition of glycine to various aldehydes.
the development and application of supramolecular bilayer membranes as artificial enzymes.
the development of a new type of supramolecular catalyst, which is based on the formation of artificial enzymes by the self-assembly of functionalized bilayer membranes.

the enantioselective aldolation of glycinaldehyde with benzaldehyde mediated by the supramolecular bilayer assembly composed of the two peptide lipids and the hydrophobic pyridoal derivative is a model reaction of the enzymatic aldolation mediated by pyridoxal-dependent enzymes.

the present system is an artificial enzyme that catalyzes the aldol condensation reaction of aldehydes with glycine to give the corresponding amino acid derivatives in high yield and with high enantioselective.
